blocks.explanation:
Is G.P. ke terms complex numbers hain, lekin G.P. ka formula wohi rehta hai.
Diya kya hai? \(1 + i, 2i, -2 + 2i, \ldots\)
Find kya karna hai? 12th term.
Plan: complex division se \(r\) nikalenge, check karenge ke ratio har jore ka barabar hai, phir \(a_{12} = a_1 r^{11}\). Badi power ko aasaan karne ke liye \((1 + i)^2 = 2i\) wali chaal lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 + i, 2i, -2 + 2i, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: \(a_{12}\).
Tareeqa: Formula \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) complex terms ke liye bhi bilkul isi tarah kaam karta hai. Mushkil sirf \(r\) nikalne aur power lene mein hai, jo hum Unit 1 ke tareeqon se karenge.

\(r\) nikalein
\[r = \dfrac{2i}{1 + i} = \dfrac{2i(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)}\]
\[= \dfrac{2i - 2i^2}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 2i}{2}\]
\[= 1 + i\]
Kyun: Complex number se divide karne ke liye upar neeche denominator ke conjugate (ulta sign wala saathi) \(1 - i\) se multiply karte hain. Neeche \((1 + i)(1 - i) = 1 - i^2 = 2\) real ban jata hai. Upar \(-2i^2 = +2\) hota hai, kyunke \(i^2 = -1\).

Agle jore se \(r\) ki tasdeeq
\[(2i)(1 + i) = 2i + 2i^2 = -2 + 2i\]
Kyun: Agar \(a_2 \times r\) se \(a_3\) mil jaye to ratio har jore ka barabar hai aur sequence waqai G.P. hai. \(2i^2 = -2\), is liye \(-2 + 2i\) aaya jo teesra term hai.

\(a_{12}\) likhein
\[a_{12} = a_1 r^{11} = (1 + i)(1 + i)^{11}\]
\[= (1 + i)^{12}\]
Kyun: Yahan khoobsurat baat yeh hai ke pehla term aur ratio dono \(1 + i\) hain. Is liye \(a_n = (1 + i)(1 + i)^{n-1} = (1 + i)^{n}\), yani term ka number hi power hai.

Square ki madad se power nikalein
\[(1 + i)^2 = 1 + 2i + i^2 = 2i\]
\[(1 + i)^{12} = (2i)^{6}\]
\[= 64\, i^{6} = 64(-1) = -64\]
Kyun: 12 dafa multiply karna lamba kaam hai. Is liye \((1 + i)^{12} = \left[(1 + i)^2\right]^{6}\) likha, aur \((1 + i)^2\) sirf \(2i\) hai. Phir \((2i)^6 = 2^6 \cdot i^6 = 64\, i^6\). \(i^4 = 1\), is liye \(i^6 = i^4 \cdot i^2 = -1\).
Dhyan dein: \((2i)^6\) mein 2 ki bhi power 6 lagti hai; sirf \(i^6\) likh kar 2 bhool jana aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq: pattern se
\[a_2 = (1 + i)^2 = 2i,\quad a_3 = (2i)(1 + i) = -2 + 2i\]
Kyun: Hamara nikala hua pattern \(a_n = (1 + i)^n\) diye gaye terms wapas deta hai, is liye 12th term bhi isi se sahi aata hai: \(-64\), jo ek real number hai.
